smaloramparts.name: Saint-Malo Ramparts
smaloramparts.slogan: A granite walk above the tide, with the whole bay at your feet.
smaloramparts.line: Saint-Malo has been ringed by an urban wall since the 12th century, reinforced again for firearms in the 15th.

rennesparlement.name: Parlement de Bretagne
rennesparlement.slogan: Brittany's gilded courtroom, risen again from its own ashes.
rennesparlement.line: Begun in 1618 and opened in 1655, it burned during a fishermen's protest in February 1994 and reopened after five years of restoration.

capfrehel.name: Cap Fréhel
capfrehel.slogan: Heather, red sandstone and a lighthouse on the edge of the world.
capfrehel.line: The present lighthouse went up between 1946 and 1950 on cliffs about 70 metres high, replacing one the Germans blew up in 1944.

fortnationalsm.name: Fort National
fortnationalsm.slogan: Vauban's island fort, reached across the sand while the sea is away.
fortnationalsm.line: Built from 1689 to 1693 on Vauban's plans for Louis XIV, it can only be reached on foot at low tide.

jerzualdinan.name: Rue du Jerzual
jerzualdinan.slogan: A cobbled drop between half-timbered shopfronts, down to the Rance.
jerzualdinan.line: Rue du Jerzual and its continuation Rue du Petit Fort link Dinan's hilltop town to its harbour on the Rance.
